title: Evolutionarily informed machine learning enhances the power of predictive gene-to-phenotype relationships
genotypes: 12 maize inbreds + 11 F1 hybrids with B73, selected for NUE diversity (23 genotypes; named in text: B73, IHP1, ILP1 Illinois protein strains; full list in Supplementary Data); RNA-seq-based models built for 16 maize lines
tissue: leaf 13 subtending the top ear (sampled 2 inches from base)
growth_system: field; Urbana, Illinois, USA; Drummer silty clay loam; split-plot; seasons 2014-2016
N_treatments: 0 vs 200 kg N/ha (granular ammonium sulfate banded at V3); unfertilized plots ~60 kg N/ha from soil
other_factors: genotype (inbreds vs B73 hybrids); separate Arabidopsis experiment (18 accessions; LN 2 mM vs HN 10 mM KNO3)
timepoints_duration: N applied at V3; single leaf sampling at R1
n_libraries: NR for maize (the 108 stated libraries are Arabidopsis)
platform_layout: Illumina HiSeq 4000, SE150 (TruSeq Stranded mRNA) for maize; Arabidopsis on HiSeq 2500 SE75
repository: NCBI GEO (stated in Methods; accession number not retrievable)
other_omics: field NUE phenotyping (318 inbreds; grain and stover N); XGBoost/GENIE3 modelling; maize UniformMu mutant (Zm00001d006835) and Arabidopsis T-DNA mutant validation
key_finding: Evolutionarily conserved N-responsive genes improve machine-learning prediction of NUE; maize NF-YA homolog mutant validated in field
source_of_details: PMC full text; nature.com publisher page (2 fetches did not reach Data availability)
notes: Methods say data are in 'GEO accession' but the number was a hyperlink stripped from the PMC text - look up GEO (Cheng/Coruzzi/Moose 2021); maize library count not stated (16 lines x 2 N x 3 reps would be 96, unconfirmed); study also contains Arabidopsis RNA-seq (non-Zea); density 49,000 (inbreds) and 77,000 (hybrids) plants/ha

title: Transcriptomic and metabolomic profiles of Zea mays fed with urea and ammonium
stage_age: 5-d-old seedlings at treatment start; sampled after 1 d
growth_system: hydroponic (aerated); growth chamber (16/8 h; 220 µmol m-2 s-1; 25/20 °C)
N_treatments: -N (N-free) vs 2 mM total N as 1 mM urea (100U), 0.5 mM urea + 0.5 mM (NH4)2SO4 (50U:50A), or 1 mM (NH4)2SO4 (100A)
timepoints_duration: RNA-seq at 1 d (24 h) of treatment; metabolomics at 1 and 7 d
platform_layout: Illumina NextSeq 500, SE75 (TruSeq 2.0; IGA Technology Services)
other_omics: metabolomics (UPLC-MS; amino acids); phytohormones and cytokinins (UHPLC-MS/MS); qRT-PCR
key_finding: Urea+ammonium mixture triggers prompt root N assimilation (ZmAMT1.1a, GLN1;2, GLN1;5, GOT1, GOT3) and glycolysis/TCA transcripts
notes: no data availability statement or accession in the PMC full text and none found by web search; analysis scripts on GitHub; companion papers PMID 33774466 and 34026974 are physiology/qPCR only

title: Strigolactones and Auxin Cooperate to Regulate Maize Root Development and Response to Nitrate
tissue: whole roots (4 seedlings pooled per replicate)
stage_age: young seedlings (age NR; germinated as in Manoli et al. 2014)
growth_system: nutrient solution; growth chamber (14/10 h; 25/18 °C; 70/90% RH; 280 µmol m-2 s-1)
N_treatments: -N (N-deprived) vs +NO3- 1 mM (counter-ion NR), after 24 h of N deprivation
other_factors: chemical treatments: TIS108 2 µM (SL biosynthesis inhibitor) under -N; PCIB 10 µM (auxin antagonist) under +NO3-
timepoints_duration: 24 h in -N solution, then 24 h treatment; single sampling at 24 h
n_libraries: 12 (computed: 4 treatments x 3 reps; 11 used in DE)
platform_layout: Illumina NovaSeq 6000, PE (read length NR; TruSeq stranded mRNA; CRIBI Padova)
other_omics: strigolactone quantification (LC-MS/MS; zealactone, carlactonoic acid); lateral-root density with SL/auxin analogues and inhibitors
key_finding: Nitrate-induced lateral rooting involves inhibition of SL biosynthesis plus auxin; RNA-seq defines auxin-/SL-dependent nitrate-responsive markers
notes: no PMC full text; -P treatment used only for SL quantification, not RNA-seq; treatment IDs differ between manuscript Table 1 and Methods; manuscript cites a GEO reviewer token - confirm public release; growth system described only as 'nutrient solution'

title: Increased biomass accumulation in maize grown in mixed nitrogen supply is mediated by auxin synthesis
stage_age: seedlings (transplanted at one expanded leaf, endosperm removed); 12 d of treatment
growth_system: hydroponic (aerated modified Hoagland, pH 5.8); growth chamber (28/22 °C; 400 µmol m-2 s-1; 60% RH)
N_treatments: 1 mM total N: NO3- alone (KNO3) vs 75% NO3-/25% NH4+ vs NH4+ alone ((NH4)2SO4)
timepoints_duration: 12 d of N-form treatment (biomass harvest 12 d after transplanting); RNA-seq sampling time not explicitly stated
n_libraries: 18 (computed: 3 N forms x 2 tissues x 3 reps)
platform_layout: Illumina HiSeq 4000, PE (insert ~300 bp; read length NR; LC Sciences)
other_omics: metabolomics (LC-MS); phytohormones; amino acids; sugars and starch; enzyme activities; photosynthesis; qRT-PCR
key_finding: Mixed nitrate/ammonium increases biomass via higher photosynthesis and shikimate-pathway auxin synthesis and auxin-response gene induction
notes: metabolomics raw data and supplementary tables on Dryad; one Methods sentence words the preliminary ratio ambiguously, but treatments are 75%/25% NO3-/NH4+ per abstract and figure legends

title: Low nitrogen availability inhibits the phosphorus starvation response in maize (Zea mays ssp. mays L.)
genotypes: W22 (wild-type segregants from a family segregating for a mutation)
growth_system: sand in PVC tubes (15 cm x 50 cm) with solid-phase alumina-P buffer; greenhouse
N_treatments: Full 1750 µM NO3- vs LowN 157.5 µM NO3- (1/3-strength Hoagland; KNO3/Ca(NO3)2 substituted with KCl/CaCl2)
other_factors: P: Full 333 µM vs LowP 10 µM KH2PO4 (alumina-P loaded with 209 vs 11 µM); 2x2 factorial (Full, LowN, LowP, LowNP)
timepoints_duration: treatments from 10 DAE (200 ml every third day, as in the growth experiment); harvest 25 DAE
platform_layout: Illumina HiSeq 4000 (UC Berkeley) and NextSeq 550 (Labsergen); TruSeq RNA v2; read layout NR
other_omics: ionomics (ICP-MS); growth and root architecture (GiA Roots); qRT-PCR (N-dose experiment)
key_finding: Low N dominates combined N+P stress, suppressing phosphate-starvation-response genes; mild N reduction suffices to repress PSR
notes: separate N-dose experiment (N 157.5, 233, 350, 875, 1750 µM x P 10 or 333 µM; 25 DAE) analysed by qRT-PCR/ionomics only, not RNA-seq; mutant name not given in retrieved text; low replication (n=2)

title: Plant Foraging Strategies Driven by Distinct Genetic Modules: Cross-Ecosystem Transcriptomics Approach
genotypes: 11 genotypes (named in text: P2023, LG2533, Canberra 90EX, P2088; full list in supplementary table)
tissue: roots (primary, lateral, seminal and crown roots; nodal roots excluded) from a 30 x 30 cm area to 20 cm depth
growth_system: field; 5 US Corn Belt sites (IL, IN, IA, NE, TX) in 2017 (66 plants); 17 plots at 7 Japanese sites in 2018 (185 plants)
N_treatments: not experimentally manipulated; natural/management gradient of soil NO3-N 10.5-212 mg/kg; leaf N measured; soil NH4-N mostly <10 mg/kg
other_factors: soil P (Bray II-P 5.3-494 mg P/kg); site, soil and climate; genotype; AM fungal colonisation
platform_layout: Illumina NextSeq 500, SE75 (KAPA Stranded mRNA-Seq; >10 M reads/sample)
repository: NCBI (accession numbers stripped from retrieved text)
other_omics: soil chemistry; leaf N and P; rRNA-seq of AM fungal community; de novo AM fungal transcript assembly
key_finding: Field root co-expression modules: mycorrhizal module induced by low P and N; PSR module mainly by low P
notes: BORDERLINE INCLUSION: observational multi-site survey, N supply not experimentally varied (N status from soil NO3-N and leaf N); Data Availability Statement says reads were deposited at NCBI (mRNA-Seq 251 samples; rRNA-seq 20 samples) but the accession numbers were hyperlinks lost from the PMC text - check the Frontiers article page

title: Comparative Transcriptome Analysis Reveals Common and Developmental Stage-Specific Genes That Respond to Low Nitrogen in Maize Leaves
tissue: sixth leaf: division zone (0-5 mm from base), elongation zone (25-45 mm from base), maturation zone (50-150 mm from tip)
stage_age: seedlings; LN imposed at V3; sixth leaf sampled (date NR)
growth_system: hydroponic (aerated); growth chamber (28/22 °C; 250-300 µmol m-2 s-1; 14/10 h)
N_treatments: HN 4.0 mM NO3- vs LN 40 µM NO3- (CaCl2 added to balance Ca)
timepoints_duration: LN from V3 (~6 d after transfer to full-strength HN solution); sampling time after treatment NR
platform_layout: Illumina HiSeq 2500, PE (insert ~125 bp; read length NR)
key_finding: Low-N-responsive genes are largely leaf-zone specific; 170 common genes enriched in photosynthesis and C/N metabolism
notes: retrieved PMC text lacks back matter (no Data Availability Statement seen) and web search found no accession; 160 HN and 240 LN plants grown; same group (Mi G) as Wang2019

title: GWAS and Transcriptome Analysis Reveal Key Genes Affecting Root Growth under Low Nitrogen Supply in Maize
genotypes: B73 (RNA-seq); 213 inbreds from 5 heterotic groups phenotyped for GWAS only
tissue: primary root (S1-S3); S0 = germinated seedlings (tissue NR)
stage_age: S0 = 48-h germinated seedlings; S1-S3 = 1, 2, 3 d after transfer
growth_system: paper-roll system in nutrient solution (hydroponic); GWAS experiment in greenhouse, Yangzhou University, 2019
N_treatments: CK 1 mM Ca(NO3)2 (2 mM NO3-) vs LN 0 mM Ca(NO3)2 (Ca balanced with CaCl2)
timepoints_duration: S0 (pre-treatment) and 1, 2, 3 d under CK or LN
bio_reps: 3 (>=6 primary roots pooled; S0: 10 seedlings pooled)
platform_layout: Illumina HiSeq, PE (TruSeq RNA; read length NR)
other_omics: GWAS (213 inbreds; GBS 361,922 SNPs); 28 root/shoot traits; ZmNAC36 targeted resequencing; qRT-PCR
key_finding: GWAS plus root RNA-seq prioritise 51 candidates; ZmNAC36 promoter variants associate with primary-root traits under low N
notes: 21 libraries = S0 x 3 + 3 timepoints x 2 N x 3 reps; GWAS phenotyping (CK vs LN for 12 d) had no RNA-seq

title: Global gene expression profiling under nitrogen stress identifies key genes involved in nitrogen stress adaptation in maize (Zea mays L.)
genotypes: DMI 56 (low-N tolerant); DMI 81 (low-N susceptible); tropical inbreds from ICAR-IIMR
growth_system: hydroponic (modified Hoagland, renewed every 3 d); greenhouse (30/22 °C; 40-50% RH)
N_treatments: N-sufficient Hoagland vs N-deficient (KNO3, Ca(NO3)2 and NH4H2PO4 replaced by K2SO4, CaCl2 and KH2PO4); working N concentrations NR
bio_reps: none evident (1 library per genotype x N x tissue)
platform_layout: Illumina (instrument and read layout NR; NxGenBio, Delhi)
key_finding: Tolerant DMI 56 shows higher NRT2.2/2.5, GS, ASNS, MYB36 and AP2-EREBP expression than susceptible DMI 81 under low N
notes: Data availability section not present in retrieved PMC text and no accession found by web search; unreplicated design (8 libraries, 63.51 Gb total)

title: Massive Loss of DNA Methylation in Nitrogen-, but Not in Phosphorus-Deficient Zea mays Roots Is Poorly Correlated With Gene Expression Differences
growth_system: hydroponic; climate chamber (16 h 25 °C / 8 h 20 °C; 400 µmol m-2 s-1; 60-80% RH)
N_treatments: control 2.5 mM Ca(NO3)2 vs -N 90 µM Ca(NO3)2
other_factors: -P (18 µM KH2PO4; control 0.1 mM rising to 0.5 mM) as a separate single-factor treatment
timepoints_duration: deficiency started ~1 wk after germination; harvest 5 wk after germination (4 wk of treatment)
other_omics: RRBS DNA methylome (HiSeq 2000 PE100, same roots); leaf N and P
key_finding: N deficiency causes massive CG/CHG hypomethylation (mostly TEs) in roots, poorly correlated with expression changes
notes: SRP135301 is stated for 'raw data'; whether it holds both RNA-seq and RRBS is not specified
